To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a cys-loop chloride ion channel is required for the chloride permeability that mediates hormone-stimulated fluid secretion in D. melanogaster.
the cys-loop ion channels are necessary for hormone-induced fluid secretion and that these channels may have evolved to control membrane permeability in secretory epithelia.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular mechanisms that underlie the control of ion and water movement in the body, and the discovery that a cys-loop channel mediates the action of a hormone on a secretory epithelium is important because it suggests that the mechanisms of ion transport and neurotransmission are related.
how animals regulate their body fluid balance and how the mechanisms of this regulation evolved.
the mechanisms of hormone-mediated fluid secretion in D. melanogaster and other insects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we discovered a cys-loop chloride ion channel, secCl, that is necessary and sufficient for chloride conductance that is activated by the Drosophila diuretic hormone DH44.
secCl, a cys-loop receptor, is necessary and sufficient for the chloride conductances that mediate hormone-induced fluid secretion.
we have discovered a new function for a pentameric cys-loop ion channels, which is to mediate hormone-induced fluid secretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified and characterized a novel chloride channel, secCl, which is essential for the fluid secretion in the Drosophila salivary gland and Malpighian tubules.
we have identified the chloride channel that mediates the effects of the insect diuretic hormone.

we discovered that secCl, a cys-loop chloride ion channel, is required for the hormone-induced transepethelial chloride conductance that controls fluid secretion in the Malpighian tubules of Drosophila.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same molecular machinery can be used for different functions in different tissues, and that evolution has coopted the same molecular components to perform different functions.
the cys-loop channel, secCl, is a key component of the hormone-induced chloride conductance of the Malpighian (renal) tubules of Drosophila melanogaster.
the same molecular machinery that controls the permeability of neurons can also control the permeability of secretory epithelial cells.
